\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{شرط} \fa{اینکه} (be shart-e inke)}{به شرط اینکه (be shart-e inke)}]{\fa{به} \fa{شرط} \fa{اینکه} (be shart-e inke) — provided that, on condition that}

\label{lesson:FA-C390-be-shart-e-inke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for violence, then the Persian for addiction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{شرط} \fa{اینکه}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{شرط} \fa{اینکه}} (\emph{be shart-e inke}) — \textquotedblleft{}provided that, on condition that\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{میآیم،} \fa{به} \fa{شرط} \fa{اینکه} \fa{زود} \fa{برگردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{miâyam, be shart-e inke zud bargardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I will come, provided that we come back early.
\end{quote}

It takes the subjunctive: \emph{be shart-e inke} + \emph{bargardim}. With a noun: \emph{be shart-e} … .

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{شرط} \fa{اینکه}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}on the condition that\textquotedblright{}: \emph{shart} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{sharṭ} \textquotedblleft{}condition\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), and \emph{be} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} and \emph{inke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} (\emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{} + \emph{ke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}) are Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be shart-e inke}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be shart-e inke}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be shart-e inke}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for violence, then the Persian for addiction, then say \emph{be shart-e inke} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{صورتی} \fa{که} (dar surati ke)}{در صورتی که (dar surati ke)}]{\fa{در} \fa{صورتی} \fa{که} (dar surati ke) — in the event that, if}

\label{lesson:FA-C390-dar-surati-ke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for addiction, then the Persian for provided that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{صورتی} \fa{که}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{صورتی} \fa{که}} (\emph{dar surati ke}) — \textquotedblleft{}in the event that, if\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{صورتی} \fa{که} \fa{باران} \fa{بیاید،} \fa{در} \fa{خانه} \fa{میمانیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar surati ke bârân biyâyad, dar khâne mimânim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, we will stay at home.
\end{quote}

It takes the subjunctive, like \emph{agar}, and sounds more formal. With the indicative it can also mean \textquotedblleft{}whereas\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{صورتی} \fa{که}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}in a form that\textquotedblright{}: \emph{surat} comes from Arabic \emph{ṣūra} \textquotedblleft{}form, image\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), here a state of affairs, and \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} are Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar surati ke}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dar surati ke}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for addiction, then the Persian for provided that, then say \emph{dar surati ke} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{صورت} (dar surat-e)}{در صورت (dar surat-e)}]{\fa{در} \fa{صورت} (dar surat-e) — in case of, in the event of}

\label{lesson:FA-C390-dar-surat-e}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for provided that, then the Persian for in the event that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{صورت}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{صورت}} (\emph{dar surat-e}) — \textquotedblleft{}in case of, in the event of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{صورت} \fa{نیاز،} \fa{دکتر} \fa{به} \fa{خانه} \fa{میآید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar surat-e niyâz, doktor be khâne miâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If needed, the doctor comes to the house.
\end{quote}

It takes a noun with ezafe: \emph{dar surat-e niyâz} \textquotedblleft{}if needed\textquotedblright{}, \emph{dar surat-e bârân} \textquotedblleft{}if it rains\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{صورت}} joins the Persian preposition \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} to \emph{surat}, from Arabic \emph{ṣūra} \textquotedblleft{}form, image\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): in the shape of, in the case of.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مگر} \fa{اینکه} (magar inke)}{مگر اینکه (magar inke)}]{\fa{مگر} \fa{اینکه} (magar inke) — unless}

\label{lesson:FA-C390-magar-inke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for in the event that, then the Persian for in case of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مگر} \fa{اینکه}}
\textbf{\fa{مگر} \fa{اینکه}} (\emph{magar inke}) — \textquotedblleft{}unless\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فردا} \fa{میرویم،} \fa{مگر} \fa{اینکه} \fa{برف} \fa{بیاید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fardâ miravim, magar inke barf biyâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We will go tomorrow, unless it snows.
\end{quote}

It takes the subjunctive: \emph{magar inke} + \emph{biyâyad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مگر} \fa{اینکه}} is native Persian, built from \emph{magar}, which EtymDB traces to a Middle Persian phrase glossed \textquotedblleft{}perhaps; lest\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{inke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{غیر} \fa{این} \fa{صورت} (dar gheyr-e in surat)}{در غیر این صورت (dar gheyr-e in surat)}]{\fa{در} \fa{غیر} \fa{این} \fa{صورت} (dar gheyr-e in surat) — otherwise, if not}

\label{lesson:FA-C390-dar-gheyr-e-in-surat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for in case of, then the Persian for unless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{غیر} \fa{این} \fa{صورت}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{غیر} \fa{این} \fa{صورت}} (\emph{dar gheyr-e in surat}) — \textquotedblleft{}otherwise, if not\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{باید} \fa{پول} \fa{را} \fa{تا} \fa{فردا} \fa{بدهد،} \fa{در} \fa{غیر} \fa{این} \fa{صورت} \fa{جریمه} \fa{میشود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bâyad pul râ tâ fardâ bedahad, dar gheyr-e in surat jarime mishavad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He must pay by tomorrow; otherwise he will be fined.
\end{quote}

A formal \emph{vagarna}; a whole clause follows.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{غیر} \fa{این} \fa{صورت}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}in other than this form\textquotedblright{}: \emph{gheyr} comes from Arabic \emph{ghayr} \textquotedblleft{}other than\textquotedblright{} and \emph{surat} from Arabic \emph{ṣūra} \textquotedblleft{}form\textquotedblright{} (both in EtymDB), held together by the Persian words \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} and \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
